appraisal_events.evidence: "Celle à qui on donne tout est si vite remplacée par une autre..."; "Il est certain qu'elle avait représenté tout autre chose pour moi, à Balbec... dans celle qui n'est plus pour nous qu'un moyen et un chemin vers d'autres..."
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly reflects that Albertine, once an object of intense desire and anguish at Balbec, has become merely a convenient, replaceable companion enlisted to help him prepare his rendezvous with another woman, reducing her local standing to instrumental usefulness.

status_effects.explanation: Albertine's romantic significance to the narrator is markedly reduced in this passage: she is treated as an interchangeable, useful helper for practical errands rather than as a desired object, in explicit contrast to her earlier importance at Balbec.
The narrator's generalizing remark that anyone given everything is quickly replaced by another frames Albertine as easily substitutable, lowering her overall local valuation.

ambiguities: The narrator's generalizing reflection on intimacy creating social bonds that 'survive love' and reduce a woman to 'a means and a path toward others' is presented as a psychological law and applied to Albertine partly through free indirect generalization; it is not fully certain whether the passage endorses this diminishment straightforwardly or frames it with some self-aware, mildly ironic distance toward the narrator's own capriciousness.

The passage's 'Mme de Stermaria' does not exactly match any alias on the reference sheet (which lists only 'M. de Stermaria' and 'Mlle de Stermaria'); she plausibly corresponds to the same young woman as the sheet's 'Mlle de Stermaria' entry, but this identity is not established by an explicit alias match, so she is recorded here as an unresolved surface form.
